boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Collierville record (November 3, 1863) in Operations on the Memphis & Charleston Railroad [November 1863]. The morning capture of the Quinn's Mill picket, the evening stand at Coldwater, the November 4 pursuit and the other Collierville actions of 1863 are outside this record or not established as within it. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force field gives the 3rd Cavalry Brigade (850) against a cavalry division (2,500); the live field reads zero. Hatch says his force engaged at Collierville was about 850 men, and that Chalmers commanded seven regiments and six guns. Chalmers says his scouts reported only one Union cavalry regiment at Collierville, but that at the first fire he found infantry, artillery and cavalry in position.
claims.rationale: Hatch's 850 matches the frozen Union bound; no inspected source gives a Confederate count. The imported bounds are unchanged and not validated.

Chalmers says he found the enemy behind intrenchments and later crossed back over Coldwater, where Hatch says the Confederates held a position almost impregnable until after dark.
claims.rationale: The stockade's construction date is not established; positions from interested accounts. No map verification.

claims.value: Chalmers says Johnston ordered him to harass Sherman's rear and break the railroad; he proposed a demonstration on Germantown or Collierville to draw off the Union cavalry, then changed his plan and attacked Collierville. NPS says the raid was meant to break up the railroad behind Sherman's corps.
claims.rationale: Stated aims from the Confederate commander and a summary; not a causal estimate.

claims.value: Hatch says he ordered Trafton into the stockade, brought the Second Iowa up dismounted and had the Sixth Illinois charge the enemy's flank attack. Chalmers says that on discovering the true force he decided at once to withdraw, and that Colonel George rode into the town without the main body of his regiment following. The frozen and live commanders are Colonel Edward Hatch and Brigadier General James R. Chalmers.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested accounts; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields give 155 (US 60; CS 95). Hatch says his loss would not exceed 60 and that he captured 50 prisoners and 7 officers. Chalmers gives his loss at Collierville as 6 killed, 63 wounded and 26 prisoners ('misoners' in OCR); his casualty return's grand total reads 95. He separately says his men killed 2 and captured a lieutenant and 26 men at the Quinn's Mill picket.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hatch's 60 is an upper estimate; the Quinn's Mill picket losses are a separate morning action.

open_questions: Trafton's, McCulloch's, Slemons's and Richardson's reports and Hurlbut's dispatches remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Hatch's and Chalmers's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXI, Part 1, are separate families of interested opposing commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
